b: The rush to feel happy makes us shallow.
Use feeling bad to move forward.
You don’t improve by feeling good about everything. Some frustrations, disappointments, and anxieties point the way forward.
Painful emotions serve a purpose. Read The Opposite of Happiness by George Loewenstein.
Regret invites you to reconsider past decisions.
Painful emotions might not align with reality. But they are worth exploring.
5 Ways to Turn Bad Feelings Into Useful Action
What happened just before I felt this way?
Discomfort tells you something is important.
Feelings are real. Their interpretation calls for reflection.
Anger doesn’t prove someone wronged you. Anxiety doesn’t prove danger is coming.
Ask, “What do I assume is true?”
Turn emotional energy into constructive action.
Envious? Clarify what you want to achieve.
Anxious? Identify one thing to prepare for.
Disappointed? Adjust your expectations or your approach.
Don’t celebrate feeling better until you consider the value of feeling bad.
Ask, “What will I do differently because of this experience?”
Don’t rush to comfort people. Don’t silence frustration. Don’t dismiss anxiety. Don’t explain away disappointment.
Help people find something good from feeling bad.
What benefit has come your way because you learned from painful emotions?
